title: sha256_file reads to EOF with no size/type check: ea_non_iid hangs forever on /dev/zero, /dev/urandom, or a FIFO
body:
## Summary

`sha256_file` (`cpp/shared/TestRunUtils.h:100-116`) reads the input to EOF with no size or type check, so pointing the tool at a non-regular file that never reaches EOF (`/dev/zero`, `/dev/urandom`, a FIFO) hangs it indefinitely before any analysis begins.

## Location

```c
// TestRunUtils.h, sha256_file
while(!feof(file)) {
    bytesRead = fread(buffer, 1, bufSize, file);
    ...
    EVP_DigestUpdate(mdctx, buffer, bytesRead);
}
```

`sha256_file` is called from `non_iid_main.cpp:180`, before `read_file_subset` and before the "Opening file" line is printed, so the hang happens with no output at all.

## Reproduction

Built at `87c104d`.

```
timeout 6 ./ea_non_iid /dev/zero      ; echo "exit=$?"   # exit=124 (still running), no output
timeout 6 ./ea_non_iid /dev/urandom   ; echo "exit=$?"   # exit=124
timeout 6 ./ea_non_iid bin/truerand_8bit.bin ; echo "exit=$?"  # exit=0 (returns) -- control
```

## Impact

Denial of service from a file-path argument alone when the path is a character device or pipe. Low severity (a regular sample file is finite), but the read is unbounded and the tool gives no indication it is stuck. `read_file_subset` has the same shape via `fseek(SEEK_END)`/`ftell`, which return 0/fail on such inputs rather than looping, so the hang is specifically the hash pass.

## Suggested fix (not submitted as code)

Stat the path and refuse anything that is not a regular file, or cap the number of bytes hashed/read.

Found during a memory-safety / robustness audit.
